messages:
maria_r: Heads up — sketching a followup to the continuous-batching RFC. want to capture a few design tradeoffs we didn't land on: admission surface vs. queue-side shaping, cache warming, and graceful preemption. posting ideas for bikeshedding.
akash_k: +1. can you summarize the new constraints?
maria_r: tl;dr: workloads are diverging — lots of tiny (<=6 tokens) bursty requests and large streaming chat. current single-shaper approach either bloats latency for small requests or wastes GPU cycles. need an evolution that keeps continuous batching benefits but reduces tail for small/interactive.
linh_t: are we looking at lane separation (tiny-fast vs packable) or a single admission API with adaptive routing?
maria_r: leaning toward a thin "queue ecosystem" layer: admission API + routing policies + per-queue shaping. the runtime batcher remains responsible for packing/dispatching; the new layer handles classifying, headroom tokens, and warmup hints.
sam_sre: major ops concern is observability and escape hatches. if we add another layer it must expose clear metrics and a kill-switch per-tenant/queue.
akash_k: agree. also need deterministic fallback: if packer is overloaded we should be able to route to a fastpath (unbatched or tiny-microbatch) without losing KV-cache affinity semantics.
maria_r: exact. thoughts on headroom signaling? idea: admission issues an opaque "slot token" (string) when enqueued; slot token is returned on dispatch completion and can be used to decide to keep/warm KV entries on the worker. slot token also carries a short-lived priority marker.
linh_t: brief nit: carry too much state and we risk coupling admission to worker internals. keep slot token opaque — workers interpret it for warming but admission shouldn't encode cache hints.
akash_k: agreed. implementation sketch:
```
// admission.go
Enqueue(req) -> EnqueueResult{slot_token: "s:abc123", queue_tag: "fast", admit_info: "n"}
// worker receives slot_token and may call KVManager.Pin(slot_token) for warming
```

sam_sre: will need metrics: enqueues, rejects, fastpath-routed, avg-wait-per-queue, headroom-utilization, slot-token-cache-hits. Can we add a per-queue circuit-breaker metric?
maria_r: yes. circuit-breaker per-queue that trips to fastpath when expected wait > threshold. fallback is explicit: worker-level fastpath that uses a short-lived unbatched execution.
akash_k: tradeoff: fastpath reduces latency but increases cost (no packing). prefer to only route to fastpath when SLOs demand it. suggestion: probabalistic fastpath for burst smoothing (e.g., 5% when queue length grows rapidly) to avoid systemic spikes.
linh_t: curious about preemption. proposal: soft-preempt handshake where admission can mark an inflight batch as "evictable" with a TTL. worker then tries to split and re-enqueue remaining tokens. sounds messy.
maria_r: prefer an opportunistic preempt: worker exposes DrainHint(batch_id) and admission can request early flush if a high-priority tenant appears. worker chooses whether to honor based on pipeline cost. avoids strong coupling.
sam_sre: we should also define failure modes: what happens if slot_token is lost mid-dispatch? fallback should treat as cold execution. document that explicitly.
akash_k: yes — if slot_token absent, worker cannot rely on KV pins; that path must be instrumented as 'cold-exec' and scheduled differently for warmup.
maria_r: another angle: admission should be workload-aware — allow callers to pass `latency_hint` and `cache_hint` fields. but defaults must be conservative.
linh_t: vendors/enterprise question — for Dedicated/Private deployments, we may want tenant-specific routing policies. surface should accept a `policy_id` or allow server-side overrides.
maria_r: plan for rollout: 1) implement admission shim behind feature flag that only classifies + emits metrics (no routing changes). 2) enable queue tagging to route a small %, 3) enable slot_token warmup path and observe cache-hit delta, 4) enable circuit-breakers and fastpath for canary tenants.
sam_sre: +1. ops checklist: feature flag per-region, per-pool, safe kill-switch that forces all routing to legacy path, and dashboards for fastpath cost delta.
akash_k: perf concerns: the shim must be extremely cheap (sub-ms) — otherwise it defeats purpose. implement in C++/Rust hotspot; keep admission state in shared memory per process to avoid RPCs.
maria_r: good call. also need to avoid stampeding warmups: if many slot_tokens arrive for a model, warmup work should be deduplicated. suggest a short dedupe window keyed by model+slot_token_prefix.
linh_t: for dedupe, also cap warmup concurrency to N per-GPU to avoid interference.
sam_sre: ops: add alert for warmup-surge and a throttling knob.
maria_r: decision tentatively: build a minimal admission shim with opaque slot_token + queue tags + metrics + circuit-breaker; no hard preempt API in v1. rely on DrainHint/early-flush opt-in for now.
akash_k: that's reasonable. can we get a quick API sketch to lock in names?
maria_r: sure — proposed HTTP/GRPC admission surface:
```
POST /v1/admit
body: { model: string, size_tokens: int, latency_hint?: "interactive" | "batch", cache_hint?: "warm" | "none", policy_id?: string }
resp: { enqueued: bool, slot_token?: string, queue_tag: string, expected_wait_ms: int }
```

linh_t: API looks good. minor: rename `latency_hint` -> `urgency` to avoid colliding with UX hints.
maria_r: updated in notes.
sam_sre: next steps for docs: update runbook with fallback steps and put a short paragraph in incident playbook about fastpath cost spikes.
akash_k: I'll prototype the in-process shim with a simple probabilistic router and expose metrics via /metrics.
maria_r: I'll write the RFC follow-up doc describing the queue ecosystem, API, rollout steps, and ops checklist. pls comment on the draft by EOD.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag created: ff/queue-ecosystem-v1 in staging.
linh_t: thanks. one more ask: include an evaluation harness to run hit-rate sims (workload mix generator) so we can quantify cost vs latency before rollout.
maria_r: yes adding that to my PR. thanks all. :thumbsup:
